posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
I try to only give advice when there is something that the player could have done that was strictly better than what they did do.  Even then, if the difference is a few hp or something else minor (like a Summon Staff), then I might not mention it because it's not worth the hassle to rewind.

 

For example, AA using the Lyre + Supertonic to get an extra Inventive Preparation before using their main power usage.  Strictly better, and very useful.

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
If there's a significant pause on a turn I will suggest a card/power (via the ultra annoying beep), I don't think that's alpha gamer mentality.

And occassionaly I will ask/suggest things in chat on how to handle a particularly deadly situation we are in but suggesting a move is not the same thing as controlling a player's action.

 

I have seen lots of "sub-optimal" plays (Why would you play a Legacy Ring against Dawn when you have 3 other good cards in hand and no extras powers, not even on the cards in hand?!) since the multiplayer started up (and none that I can remember in real world play, although I'm sure there were) and while I might silently seethe on the other side of my computer I have not expressed this in game.

 

EDIT: Also, isn't suggesting things to other players a way of teaching an intricacy of the game that they might have previously missed? (I taught someone the Prejudice, Pride, Prejudice combo on the app recently).

posts.name: Pydro
posts.cooked:
I made two suggestions to the Trello board about this:

1) Have in the config (so you can turn on and off) a delay to suggestions. This way someone doesn't instantly tell someone what to do, and you have a chance to look around at what's what.

2) A "help me" button where you are telling everyone that you want suggestion for this play.

So, I learned that you should never play Matriarch on multiplayer.

 

Matriarch is bad enough when one person has to click through everything.  When you have to depend on multiple people (and possibly the communication lag), it takes forever.

 

We had about a dozen birds get wiped out with a Carrion Fields and Stealth Bot out.  Fortunately Heroic Interception meant that only Legacy's damage prompted a Stealth Bot question, or I'd still be in that game wading through check boxes.

Agreed.  I don't know how many times I've chosen the wrong power on Tempest's Hurricane by accident.

 

 

Some of the features I've suggested for multiplayer:
A way to undo suggestions

A voting option that would allow a single player to 'filibuster' and stop the 'choose for me' option if they care about the ordering, but no one else does (optimizing Decoy Projection, etc)

An option to allow incapped players to see other player's hands in close hand games.

The ability to rewind within your turn without needing the permission of the other players

An optional notification beep to tell you when you have to make a decision
